clue.text: Composer's coach initially lectured on Ring: "Wagner's finale very loud!"

parts.note: a coach is a railway carriage, or car

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: opening letter of the word
the letter O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: a finale is the closing part, so only the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: closing letter of the composer's name
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A music coach lectures on Wagner's Ring cycle and praises its thunderous ending.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ring here is just the letter O, not Wagner's opera cycle, which the surface pushes hard. Carl Orff wrote Carmina Burana.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Orff was a twentieth-century German musician best known for the choral work Carmina Burana.

clue.text: Mountain resort songbird?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ski resort in the mountains of British Columbia, Canada
second meaning, playful: anyone who makes tunes with pursed lips; the question mark flags the stretch

explanation.walkthrough: One of the nine themed answers: all are painters, here James McNeill Whistler. 'Songbird' is a whimsical description of a person producing a tune by blowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Whistler is a well-known Canadian ski destination, and literally someone who whistles a melody, loosely a singing bird.

clue.text: See 1
Great poet and dramatist's second scary film?

parts.note: s is the standard abbreviation for second
a chiller is a frightening film or story

explanation.surface: A celebrated writer follows up with another frightening movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' reads as 'his next', but it only supplies its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Schiller was a major German writer of verse and stage plays, author of the Ode to Joy.

clue.text: Fancy getting a rise — about $1,000 — sir?

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading from bottom to top, so the word is turned around
about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to fancy is to think or suppose
a grand, a thousand dollars, is G

explanation.surface: Someone asks their boss, deferentially, whether a thousand-dollar pay rise might be on the cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sir' looks like a polite address but is the title a knight holds. Laura Knight is the themed painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight is entitled to be called Sir, so the title stands as an example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Old jacket on male roué with top missing gets a delayed reaction

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, and missing means it is gone

parts.note: a doublet is a close-fitting jacket worn by men in Tudor times
a rake is a dissolute man, a roué

explanation.surface: An old libertine in period dress is slow to react to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just places the jacket before the rake in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A double take is a second, startled look at something whose significance was not grasped the first time.

clue.text: Spin merchant, Tina?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who spins things round, such as a lathe worker
second meaning: the singer Tina, by her surname; the question mark marks her as one example

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin merchant' suggests a political spin doctor, but it is just someone who turns. The themed painter is J. M. W. Turner.
explanation.definitionFit: A turner shapes wood or metal on a rotating lathe, and Tina Turner is the famous rock singer.

clue.text: Live two lives as an inventor?

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
L marks the live wire on a plug, and two of them make LL

explanation.surface: Someone leads a double life while posing as an inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for live as in a live wire. Vanessa Bell is the themed painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Graham Bell is credited with creating the telephone; the question mark marks him as one example.

clue.text: Hate Arab horse having its wings clipped

indicators.note: clipping wings trims both sides, leaving only the inner letters of the phrase

parts.note: the phrase with two letters trimmed from each end

explanation.surface: A thoroughbred desert steed is resentful about being clipped.
explanation.walkthrough: The wings are the outer two letters on each side of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor is to loathe or detest, a strong verb synonym.

clue.text: Count, smitten with love, twisted like a bud

indicators.note: smitten means struck, and the struck letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nobleman, head over heels in love, is all of a twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a nobleman or a verb, and 'smitten with love' reads as infatuated; both words are raw letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Convolute is a botanical term for leaves or petals rolled up together inside an unopened shoot.

clue.text: Endure a dance, an old person's affair?

parts.note: to last is to endure or keep going
the Highland fling is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: An elderly person stays on their feet through a dance and enjoys a final romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Fling has two senses here: the dance, and a brief romance, which feeds the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A last fling is a final spell of enjoyment or romance before settling down, apt for someone ageing.

clue.text: Stock bar with booze (third off)

indicators.note: the third letter is taken off, counting along the word

parts.note: to bar is to ban or forbid
ale is beer, a kind of booze

explanation.surface: A pub stocks its bar with drink, but a third of it is off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' and 'bar' sound like pub business; 'stock' is the adjective meaning standard, and 'bar' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock as an adjective means commonplace or trite, like a stock phrase, which matches banal.

clue.text: Paper bundle: energy-deficient power source that's injurious

indicators.note: lacking energy means the abbreviation for energy is removed

parts.note: a bale is a large bundle of paper, conventionally ten reams
fuel is a source of power

explanation.surface: A bundle of paper burnt for power without much energy proves harmful.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the physics symbol for energy, so that letter leaves the power source.
explanation.definitionFit: Baleful means harmful or menacing, so it can replace injurious as an adjective.

clue.text: Food conveyance up and working

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a cab is a taxi, a means of conveyance
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A food delivery vehicle is up and running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up and working' reads like a single phrase, but 'up' is the reversal signal. Francis Bacon is the themed painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon is cured pork, an example of something to eat, so the general word covers it.

clue.text: Front opening gives a bias to boxers etc.

parts.note: the fly is the opening at the front of trousers
to weight something is to load it, giving a bias

explanation.surface: A gap in the front of the boxer shorts makes them hang lopsided.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxers suggests underpants with a front opening, but they are fighters.
explanation.definitionFit: Flyweights are competitors in the lightest weight class, in boxing and other combat sports, hence 'etc.'.

clue.text: The opposition eating flipping eggs? Prove it!

indicators.note: what is eaten ends up inside the eater, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: them is the other side, as in us and them

indicators.note: flipping something tosses it about, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: roe is fish eggs

explanation.surface: Someone claims their opponents are tossing eggs in a pan and is challenged to show proof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British curse or a pancake toss, but it rearranges the eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a mathematical statement that must be proved, so 'Prove it!' playfully stands for one.

clue.text: Masses welcoming new champ

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in a guest, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: much means a great deal, masses
n is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Crowds turn out to greet a new title holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champ' looks like a champion, but it is the verb meaning to chew. Edvard Munch is the themed painter.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ is to chew noisily, and to munch is likewise to chew steadily and audibly.

clue.text: Dish of dog fish (gutted)

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, leaving only the outer letters of a word

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish; only its outer letters remain

explanation.surface: A meal made of dog and cleaned fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The fish is the ray, with its middle letter cut out.
explanation.definitionFit: A curry is a spiced meal, one kind of dish served at a table.

clue.text: Bureaucracy's advice about bug

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: rede is an archaic word for counsel
to bug a phone is to tap it

explanation.surface: Officialdom issues guidance on dealing with an insect or a listening device.
explanation.walkthrough: Rede is old-fashioned English for advice, found in crosswords and Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Red tape is excessive official rules and paperwork, the defining vice of bureaucracy.

clue.text: Bury's opposite Pluto — and between

parts.note: Dis is another Roman name for Pluto, god of the underworld
inter- is the Latin prefix meaning between, as in international

explanation.surface: Bury, a Lancashire town, sits facing the dwarf planet with something in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the town of Bury, but it is the verb. Inter also means bury, adding a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinter is to dig up a corpse from its grave, the reverse of putting it in the ground.

clue.text: Ghostly Arthur once associated with court knight

parts.note: Arthur Ashe was a champion tennis player
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: King Arthur's pale ghost returns to haunt Camelot's court and its knights.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur and knight conjure Camelot, but the court is a tennis court and Arthur is the American player Ashe.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen describes a pale grey face, like someone who has seen a spirit, matching ghostly.

clue.text: Blooming Teddy boy dance by Prince — a rare heavenly sight!

parts.note: hale means healthy, in bloom
the bop was a dance popular with 1950s Teddy boys, British youths in Edwardian-style suits
P is the abbreviation for prince

explanation.surface: An exuberant rocker dancing to Prince is a sight seldom seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' reads like the mild British intensifier, but it means healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hale-Bopp was the bright comet visible to the naked eye in 1997, an uncommon spectacle in the night sky.

clue.text: Perhaps local injections units?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, playful: things that numb, such as local anaesthetic shots
second meaning: figures, such as ones

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as numb-ers, things that deaden feeling; 'Perhaps' marks a local anaesthetic as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A local anaesthetic numbs a body part, making it a numb-er, and units are figures counted in arithmetic.

clue.text: Grain factory on film

parts.note: a mill is a factory, as in a cotton mill
E.T. is Spielberg's film about an alien

explanation.surface: A documentary about a cereal processing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the first piece above the second. Jean-François Millet is the themed painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Millet is a small-seeded cereal crop grown for food and birdseed.

clue.text: Portion of corset elastic

indicators.note: something elastic stretches out of shape, so the letters are pulled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A section of stretchy undergarment fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Portion of' looks like a signal for letters inside a phrase, but the answer is not there; 'elastic' rearranges the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector is a part or division, such as a slice of a circle, so it means a piece.

clue.text: Nick the Unfinished's sneakiness

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to steal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cunning character styled like a medieval king, Nick the Unfinished, is known for slyness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a man's name with a royal epithet, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is secret, furtive behaviour, meaning much the same as underhand cunning.

clue.text: Camp joke about Uruguay's premier getting lost

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the others

parts.note: a gag is a joke

indicators.note: premier means first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of the country
L stands for lost in sports results tables

explanation.surface: A flamboyant joke about Uruguay's prime minister going missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp' looks like the adjective meaning flamboyant, describing the joke, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulag was the Soviet system of forced-labour prison camps, and the word now names any such camp.

clue.text: See 29
Officer responsible for politician getting second desk?

parts.note: Con is short for a Conservative politician
s is the abbreviation for second
a table can serve as a desk

explanation.surface: An official in charge of an MP who has been given a second desk.
explanation.walkthrough: John Constable is the themed painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is a police officer of the lowest rank in Britain.

clue.text: See 18
Tea before the scheduled hour holds up a work unit

indicators.note: to hold is to keep inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: early means ahead of time

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom, so letters run backwards

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Taking a tea break ahead of time holds up an office team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work unit' suggests a team at a workplace, but it is the erg from physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Earl Grey is a black tea blend flavoured with bergamot oil, named after a British prime minister.

clue.text: Conductor to-be went on horseback

parts.note: elect after a title means chosen but not yet in office, as in president-elect
past tense of ride

explanation.surface: An orchestra's next maestro arrived riding a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' looks like a maestro or a bus conductor, but it is the electrical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a terminal through which current enters or leaves a circuit, an electrical carrier.

clue.text: Cake decorator Penny put in the dock

indicators.note: to put one thing in another places it inside, between its letters

parts.note: a pier is a landing stage where boats dock
p is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: A woman named Penny who ices cakes ends up in the dock at court.
explanation.walkthrough: Penny looks like a name and the dock like a courtroom. John Piper is the themed painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is applied through a nozzle in lines called piping, so a cake icer is literally one who pipes.
